comment: Shared by rust/examples/exact_bench.rs (Ajisai, native) and scripts/bench/exact_bench.py (fractions.Fraction, SymPy, python-flint); scripts/bench/exact-bench.mjs runs both and compares. `{n}` in `source` is replaced by `n`. Each case is one exact computation whose answer every system must agree on; the runner refuses to report a time for a system whose answer differs. Each case names its computation in `kind`, which the Python and C sides implement, folding left to right as Ajisai's FOLD does. A case with `decimalDigits` also has Ajisai render its answer with that many digits of FORMAT, untimed, for a system that can only answer in decimal (FLINT's Calcium for `sqrt-sum`).

cases.name: harmonic
cases.source: 1 {n} RANGE 'K' BIND 1 K DIV 0 [ ADD ] FOLD

cases.name: basel
cases.source: 1 {n} RANGE 'K' BIND 1 K K MUL DIV 0 [ ADD ] FOLD

cases.name: newton-sqrt2
cases.what: n Newton steps x <- (x + 2/x)/2 from x = 1; the digits double each step
cases.source: 1 {n} RANGE 1 [ 'I' BIND 'X' BIND X 2 X DIV ADD 2 DIV ] FOLD

cases.name: elementwise
cases.what: the Vector of (k+1)/k * k/(k+2) for k = 1..n, element by element
cases.source: 1 {n} RANGE 'K' BIND K 1 ADD K DIV K K 2 ADD DIV MUL

cases.name: sqrt-sum
cases.what: sqrt(1) + sqrt(2) + ... + sqrt(n), exact, in square-free normal form

cases.name: sqrt-sum-1000
cases.what: sqrt(1) + sqrt(2) + ... + sqrt(n), exact, in square-free normal form
